reason: The message, block, chunk and failure vocabulary, the adapter registry, call preparation, failure normalisation, the assembler and the compact stream record are kept as the contract package llm and the runtime component; the open, plugin-extensible sets become closed Go sets.

The vendor's Messages transport is kept as the shared transport, the Anthropic Messages driver and the vendor provider package; the Files upload path, listing and version gate are kept with a time-based upload cool-down and a stored listing.

The account route keeps its single credential source, per-account listing and sign-out cancellation; cancellation no longer depends on the route component being loaded because the request header records the credential reference.
The API-key route is the first working provider; it follows the official listing through a keyed model overlay instead of comparing the configured list with the built-in one.

The library-backed multi-provider adapter is replaced by three more harness-owned protocol drivers, a keyed-route provider component and an embedded catalogue; its role as the second twin is replaced by a conformance rule.
Retry stays a listener outside the adapter that logs each retry before waiting; it now decides by failure class, has no unlimited mode, and shares one attempt cap per step.

The registry of extra request body fields becomes the request-contribution service of the shared transport, available to any route and listed per route, with every contribution off until the user opts in.
There are no npm plugin packages in Go; the field is replaced by an opt-in installation inventory contribution that reports the build version, enabled entry ids and plugin manifests.
The meter service and its three projections are kept as deterministic folds of the log with no model call; projection state is bounded and estimates are scaled by a per-session calibration factor.

Replaced by the around key llm.StreamAround, whose listeners may proceed or substitute the stream with the substitution recorded in the attempt record; rerouting a request to another provider is no longer possible.
Replaced by the payload-free notify key llm.RoutesChanged; a failing observer is contained and cannot veto a registry change, as upstream.
Replaced by the notify key llm.ModelsChanged carrying the route id, which the model picker fragment reloads on.

Replaced by the ordered key llm.PrepareHeaders, which applies to every route instead of one adapter; credential headers and the client identity are applied afterwards and an error fails the call before any I/O.
Replaced by the Go struct deepseek.AccountConfig: the same connection, listing and image fields, a keyed model overlay instead of modelOverrides, and the per-route Send settings.
Replaced by the Go struct deepseek.APIKeyConfig with a credential reference, a keyed model overlay, a listing mode and the per-route Send settings.

Replaced by the Go struct keyed.Config, a map of routes each with one protocol, an endpoint, a credential reference, headers, a model overlay, deviation switches and a retry policy; it is empty by default.
Upstream's executor config is empty; the Go struct retry.Config adds the one cap on attempts per step, and the policy itself stays on each route.
The enabled flag that defaults to true is replaced by naming the inventory contribution in a route's transport.Send settings, which default to sending nothing.
Upstream's meter config is empty; the Go struct meter.Config has one field that switches the calibration factor.
ctx.llm becomes the service key llm.RuntimeKey with the Runtime interface: register routes, list routes and models, prepare a call, and complete a buffered one-shot call.
ctx.deepseekLlmApiExtensions becomes the service key transport.ContributionsKey, where a component registers a named contributor that prepares a field and accepts delivery after HTTP 2xx.
ctx.tokenMeter becomes the service key meter.Key with Measure, Pressure and EstimateMessage.
Request contributions are registered by name and listed per route, so any route may opt in; the registry is no longer tied to one vendor route.
Contributed fields are appended in name order after the base fields, so the request bytes are reproducible and can be compared with stored expectations.
The last good listing is stored in a machine-state table keyed by endpoint and credential fingerprint and is served, marked stale, when the host starts without a network.
Every listing change notifies llm.ModelsChanged, which the model picker fragment reloads on; the upstream README body already describes an announcement, so the bullet is also stale.
The version gate is still evaluated in the client, so a modified client can still request any model id unless the vendor service rejects it.
justification: No client can enforce a rule on a modified copy of itself; enforcement belongs to the vendor service. The Go design documents the gate as a compatibility guard, not a security control. The stage is a placeholder because no implementation plan exists yet.

reason: The listing's reasoning effort levels are still not read; levels come from the embedded catalogue and can be corrected per model in the route's overlay.
justification: The field that carries effort levels is not parsed anywhere in the pinned upstream source, so its shape is unknown and cannot be designed against without the vendor's listing contract. The stage is a placeholder because no implementation plan exists yet.

reason: A listed model the build cannot drive is returned as unavailable with its reason and minimum version, so the picker can show an upgrade notice instead of a generic empty state.
Overlay fields accept an explicit none value, so an override can remove a system-prompt or tool update mode as well as set one.

The logged request header records the credential reference name and sign-out cancels every running agent whose latest header names it, so the report and the cancellation no longer depend on the route component being loaded, and a running tool is cancelled with the turn.
An on-demand route check sends one small real request per chosen model and reports the classified result, which gives the user the remote validation the configured catalogue cannot.
One resolved model set (catalogue, listing, overlay) serves the settings page, the picker and the request, so the page and the listing cannot disagree and an edit cannot drop a listed model.
Configuration is an overlay keyed by model id, so a route with edited models still receives the ids a followed listing adds later.
Nothing compares the configured models with a built-in list any more; an overlay entry is explicit, so a new build cannot turn an old default into a customisation.
The last good listing is stored in a machine-state table and served, marked stale, on a start without a network.
Every listing change notifies llm.ModelsChanged, which the model picker fragment reloads on.
Listed models the build cannot drive are returned as unavailable with a reason, so a route with no servable model explains itself instead of offering nothing.
A route's models are an overlay keyed by model id and edited per model; there is no list to replace as a whole.
Controls gains ToolChoice, and every driver either encodes it or fails with llm/unsupported-option before any I/O.
Every provider client comes from the egress factory, so model requests follow the one proxy and certificate policy and nothing uses a default transport.

When the Messages driver cannot place an in-history system update after a user or tool-result turn it consolidates the update into the leading system slot for that request and logs a diagnostic, so placement never fails a request.
Images remain input only and are never sent as URLs; only the upload-recovery part changes, from a count of skipped requests to a time-based cool-down.
justification: A URL the provider fetches would be model-visible content that is not in the session log, which outcome DH-O-4 forbids, and assistant image output is a new modality that needs UI, compaction and replay support nobody has designed. The stage is a placeholder because no implementation plan exists yet.

reason: The on-demand route check probes a chosen model against the configured gateway, and a refused model fails with a classified code instead of a guess from the catalogue.
Real-provider scenarios take the key at run time in a separate credentialed workflow, and a scenario that did not run for lack of a key is reported as open, never as passed.
The harness encodes the request body itself, so the image budget is enforced on the encoded request size and not only on the base64 image payload.
One image policy serves every driver and removes the oldest images in byte and count quanta, so an image-adding request does not restart prompt-cache reuse every time.

A pending sign-in is an interaction in the host registry, so a page reload re-attaches to it, and sign-out calls the issuer's revocation endpoint where one exists; a host restart still abandons a pending sign-in.

OAuth routes are a later provider component that can hold an opt-in installation identifier for an issuer that requires one; whether to offer a third party's consumer sign-in is recorded as an owner question.

The four protocol drivers receive credentials only from the harness credential service, so nothing reads the environment or credential files on its own; a cloud component's vendor module that reads its own chain is stated in that deliverable.
Layers are first-class: the ownership index shows which layer supplies a route, and the writable layer can remove an inherited route explicitly instead of only resetting to it.
Routes and models merge by key across layers and removal is an explicit operation, so writing one route cannot silently drop inherited entries.
A header value is plain text or a credential reference of the redacting secret type, and a plain value under a credential-bearing header name is refused when the config loads.
A route chooses its listing mode: offer keeps adoption explicit and follow lets the endpoint's listing contribute model ids.
Discovery follows the listing's pagination up to a bounded page count and reports when it stopped early, instead of reading one page.
A route speaks exactly one protocol and a vendor with two protocols is two routes, so a model the catalogue does not list is never ambiguous.
The on-demand route check probes each declared input type with a real request, so a wrong declaration is found before a conversation depends on it.
The harness's own drivers send no authentication header for a route that names no credential, so a keyless local server needs no placeholder key.
Reasoning level spellings, and whether a model can disable reasoning, are per-model catalogue data the Gemini driver reads, not a fixed list inside a library.
Each driver sends stop sequences where its protocol has them and fails before I/O where it does not.
System-prompt and tool update modes are overlay fields any route or model can set in configuration, not flags locked inside an installed catalogue.
Each driver states which roles can carry images, and an image in any other role is sent as the same placeholder text a text-only route receives instead of failing the request.
The shared transport keeps the HTTP status, headers, request id and original error, and failure class is a property of the code, so nothing is classified from message text.
No library is in the request path, so there is no library retry to switch off; one-shot callers that upstream leaves single-attempt get a buffered retry through Runtime.Complete.
The harness's own decoders forward tool-argument fragments as text and check the JSON once at the end, so there is no per-fragment re-parse and no patch to carry.
The prefix digest is computed over the request bytes actually sent, and a route may keep signed reasoning across a prefix change where its endpoint does not check.

A resolved model declares that its reasoning is bound to the request prefix, and the driver loop then holds a prefix change until the open tool round ends, which removes the cause of the rejection; this needs the agent-loop area.
Decoders keep every response member they do not model as raw JSON and replay it to the same route, so a provider-private signature survives without a patch.
Runtime.Complete applies the route's retry policy to a buffered one-shot call and exposes no chunk of a failed attempt, so callers outside the agent loop are no longer single-attempt.

Retry is decided by failure class: a permanent failure such as authentication, quota or an invalid request is never retried in any mode, and the unlimited mode is replaced by one bounded by elapsed time.
One cap on attempts per step, counted from the log, binds every recovery listener, so separate budgets no longer add up.

The retry component acts on transient failures by class without first waiting for another listener, so its outcome no longer depends on listener order; a listener that never returns is bounded by the agent-loop area's dispatch deadline.
A new durable event llm/retry-abandoned records why recovery stopped, so exhaustion and cancellation are facts in the log and not inferred from later events.
Retry is a separate component by decision, a per-route concurrency cap is added to the runtime, and a response cache is deliberately absent because it would answer without an attempt.
One client identity value is the default User-Agent of every egress client, so model requests and web tools send the same identity; this needs a default hook from the egress owner.
Controls adds TopP and ToolChoice, which all four protocols can carry, and other gateway parameters are static route configuration in extraBody.
The rule that no variant exists without a producer is kept as policy; cache breakpoints are placed by the Anthropic driver itself and need no vocabulary variant.
The block set is a closed Go set and a plugin is a process that cannot add a block type, so the assembler can never meet an unknown block.
The request carries the session as an opaque label that package llm owns, and package session imports llm and never the reverse, so there is no cycle and no duplicate declaration.
A loop request can only be built from the log, so the tool-update projection always receives the session-folded tool history and the missing-history fallback cannot arise for it.
Exists only because of npm: the limit is that some plugins have no npm package name and version. Go has no npm packages; a compiled-in component's identity is the binary's build version.
A compiled-in component always has the binary's identity and a plugin process cannot load without a manifest, so the opt-in installation inventory cannot be partial.
Exists only because Node can replace a mounted npm package in a running process; Go never replaces code in a running process, and a plugin process re-reads its manifest when it is restarted.
Token counts for text remain an estimate; the Go design reduces the error with a per-session calibration factor but does not make it exact.
justification: An exact count needs a provider tokenizer in the binary or a network call per measurement, and the meter's contract is a deterministic fold of the log with no model call. The stage is a placeholder because no implementation plan exists yet.

reason: Meter state is checkpointed in the same transaction as its events, and a cold read prices only the current surface read from the session, not the whole log.
Values are immutable by ownership, so a measurement shares them instead of cloning, and context pressure is a stored total read in constant time.
When the request envelope differs from the last measured one, the estimate is scaled by the session's calibration factor instead of falling back to the raw heuristic.
The fold keeps the price of each retained system prompt and reprices a replacement in the same step, so a rewrite is no longer counted as zero until the next usage sample.
Projection state is totals plus one price per retained system prompt; the surface has one owner, the session, and is not copied into a checkpoint.
The shared transport keeps the original transport error as the cause of the failure value, so classification uses the status and the cause instead of matching words in a flattened message.
The open question is answered: Controls is logged with each request, and provider-specific request options are route configuration, not call configuration.
Exists only because Node could replace an npm package version inside a running process, which would make cached manifest identities stale; Go never replaces code in a running process.

The second adapter for the same vendor was the npm library the Go design removes; its purpose is kept as a conformance rule: one table for four drivers, no vocabulary element that fewer than two protocol families produce, and fixtures recorded from real providers.
Failures stay serialisable facts without policy and a listener decides retry within bounds; the Go design adds a failure class per code, removes the unlimited mode and caps attempts per step.
The provider id selects the adapter, a route has one owner and a duplicate fails; the generic library backend becomes harness-owned drivers and keyed routes.
Every message gets its id at creation and keeps it through every representation; Go enforces immutability through constructors and ownership instead of a run-time freeze.

Billed usage and context occupancy stay projections of the whole log, counting failed attempts and retries once each, and occupancy stays a reference figure; the request-context event belongs to the agent-loop area.
The runtime stays the one place that turns an adapter failure into a terminal chunk, and a consumer's own error never becomes a model failure; Go adds recovery from a panic and from a missing finish.

The prepare-then-accept mechanism is kept as a transport service, but every contribution is off until the user opts in per route, which the owner's decision on data leaving the machine requires, and any route may use it.
A message's source kind names its producer in the Go vocabulary; the conversion table for older session formats is not built because upstream files are not read.
Two routes keep two credential sources with no fallback, and sign-out cancels running work that used the account, found from the logged request header and not from a second provider field.

The account listing, the row-by-row decoding and the locally evaluated version gate are kept; the last good listing is now stored and a refused model is shown as unavailable. The gate's version key is an owner question because the Go build does not share upstream's version numbers.
Projection state keeps only system prompts and a running total, and that bound is applied to every meter projection in the Go design.
The rule that the driver adapts and the log stays truthful is kept: on a model without mid-conversation system support a later system message is sent as a user-role reminder by the driver.

The official route still follows the listing only on the official origin, but the rule that a customised catalogue stops following it is replaced by a keyed overlay, which removes the comparison with the built-in list and the four limitations it causes.
A message source may declare a semantic form with the fields that form needs; it is a tag on the value in package llm, and how it looks belongs to the user-interface areas.

The vendor is reached through the Anthropic Messages protocol with lossless replay signatures, native placement of system updates and Files references for images, implemented as the first harness-owned driver.
A badge beside a model name comes from the listing and is validated on the host; it stays display data that no request, session event or tool carries.

No placeholder tool is invented for an all-deferred request; the provider's rejection is surfaced as a classified failure, because a placeholder changes the cached prefix and advertises a tool nothing runs.
Adopted by omission: the Go stream record has the first-token reader that statistics and the trajectory view need and none of the five unused visibility queries.
Exists only because of Node: the proposal and its rejection concern a Node timer helper and a JavaScript test clock. A cancellable wait in Go is a select on a timer and the context.
